plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: Nodding, saucer-shaped white blooms with golden stamens that open in the cold, often pushing up through frost and light snow. The flowers age to soft pink-green. They bring a rare burst of elegance to the dark heart of winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring, typically December through March in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Alpine and woodland regions of central and southern Europe, widely grown in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, the Christmas rose is not a rose at all. It belongs to the buttercup family, and every part of the plant is toxic.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms with layered petals and bright yellow centers. The flowers stand out against dark, leathery leaves in cool winter gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with peak bloom from December to March in mild climates
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and eastern China, and widely grown in the southeastern United States, western Europe and Japan
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, long used in Japan for hair care and cooking.

plants.name: Metrosideros excelsa
plants.description: A gnarled coastal evergreen that erupts into crimson pompom-like flowers made of bursts of long, brush-like stamens. Whole cliffs and beaches glow red as the southern summer begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer in the Southern Hemisphere, peaking in December
plants.location: Coastal North Island of New Zealand
plants.funFact: Pōhutukawa can cling to steep sea cliffs, and its flowering around Christmas has made it a beloved symbol of the New Zealand summer holidays.
